'''Hugo E. Rossi''' (born 1935)<ref>''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale 2004</ref> is an American mathematician working in [[complex analysis]].

Rossi graduated from the [[City College of New York]] with bachelor's degree in 1956, and graduated from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] with the master's degree in 1957, and received a Ph.D. under the supervision of [[Isadore Singer]] in 1960 (''Maximality of algebras of holomorphic functions'').<ref>[http://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=24027 Mathematics Genealogy Project]</ref> In 1960 he became an assistant professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], and in the same year at [[Princeton University]]. In 1963 he became an associate professor and a professor at [[Brandeis University]] in 1966. After 11 years at Brandeis and two years as the department chair, he moved to the [[University of Utah]] in 1975, and he served as dean of the [[University of Utah College of Science|College of Science]] from 1987 to 1993.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Maffly|first1=Brian|title=New U. center promotes science and math teaching|url=http://archive.sltrib.com/story.php?ref=/ci_13509833|accessdate=26 March 2017|work=The Salt Lake Tribune|date=7 October 2009}}</ref> In 1989 Rossi went on temporary leave from his post as dean to serve as director of the [[National Cold Fusion Institute]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Broad|first1=William J.|title=Despite Scorn, Team in Utah Still Seeks Cold-Fusion Clues|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1989/10/31/science/despite-scorn-team-in-utah-still-seeks-cold-fusion-clues.html|accessdate=26 March 2017|work=The New York Times|date=31 October 1989}}</ref> Amid increasing concerns about the lack of conclusive results regarding [[cold fusion]], Rossi resigned and returned to his post as dean of the College.<ref>{{cite news|title=DIRECTOR RESIGNS HIS POST WITH COLD FUSION INSTITUTE|url=http://www.deseretnews.com/article/73489/DIRECTOR-RESIGNS-HIS-POST-WITH-COLD-FUSION-INSTITUTE.html?pg=all|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170327080544/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/73489/DIRECTOR-RESIGNS-HIS-POST-WITH-COLD-FUSION-INSTITUTE.html?pg=all|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 27, 2017|accessdate=26 March 2017|work=Deseret News|agency=Associated Press|date=20 November 1989|language=en}}</ref>

From 1983 to 1984, he was at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton, New Jersey. From 1980 to 1985, he was the editor of the ''Pacific Journal of Mathematics'' and from 1973 to 1978 a co-editor of transactions of the American Mathematical Society. He is a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20121025003234/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-11-23.</ref> He served as chairman of the board of the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] from 1985 to 1989 and twice as deputy directory, from 1997 to 1995 and 2003 to 2005.<ref>{{cite web|title=The History of MSRI|url=https://www.msri.org/web/msri/pages/231|website=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|accessdate=16 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170517100204/https://www.msri.org/web/msri/pages/231|archive-date=2017-05-17|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Works ==
*Topics in complex manifolds, Presses de l´Université de Montréal 1971
*With [[Robert Gunning (mathematician)|Robert Gunning]], Analytic functions of several complex variables, Prentice-Hall 1965
*Prospects in Mathematics – Invited talks on the occasion of the 250th anniversary of Princeton University, American Mathematical Society 2008
Advanced calculus – problems and applications to science and engineering, Benjamin 1970
